_README: Per-nationality visa deep-dive: Mongolia → Korea. Grounded in official channels (Korea Visa Portal visa.go.kr; Korea Visa Application Center Mongolia = visaforkorea.mn, IOM-operated; Korean Embassy Ulaanbaatar). Fee/processing are VOLATILE (factId visa-mongolia-c39). No invented figures. Single consular jurisdiction (no jurisdiction block).
metaTitle: Mongolia to Korea Visa: Do You Need One? (2026) — Korea Trip Hub
metaDesc: Yes — Mongolian passport holders need a visa for South Korea (C-3-9 short-term tourist, up to 90 days). Apply at the Korea Visa Application Center in Ulaanbaatar: documents, fees and processing time, step by step.

verdict.headline: Yes — Mongolian passport holders need a visa.
verdict.sub: You'll apply for the C-3-9 short-term tourist visa (single entry, stay up to 90 days) in person at the Korea Visa Application Center in Ulaanbaatar. K-ETA/visa-free entry does NOT apply to Mongolian passports.
verdict.entry: Single entry (multiple-entry possible in some cases — ask at KVAC)

tldr: Fill the form at visa.go.kr (the ONLY official portal) — from 1 April 2026 it must be typed, printed and signed (handwritten forms are refused).
Submit in person at the Korea Visa Application Center (KVAC) in Ulaanbaatar — visaforkorea.mn.
Bring passport, photo, round-trip flight + hotel reservations, and a 6-month bank statement.
Fee ≈ US$40 for a single-entry short stay; result in about 5–15 business days.

items.title: Confirm the visa type
items.detail: For tourism you want the C-3-9 short-term visit (tourist) visa. Gather the checklist below before you start.

items.title: Fill the form at visa.go.kr
items.detail: Go to the Korea Visa Portal (visa.go.kr) — the only official site. Complete the form on a computer in English or Korean, then print and sign it. Since 1 April 2026 handwritten forms are not accepted. One form per applicant.

items.title: Assemble your documents
items.detail: Collect every document in the checklist below. Missing financials or a wrong-format photo are the top reasons for delays.

items.title: Submit at the KVAC in Ulaanbaatar
items.detail: Hand in your form and documents in person at the Korea Visa Application Center (visaforkorea.mn). Check its site for current hours and whether an appointment is needed.

items.title: Pay the fee
items.detail: Pay the visa fee plus the center's service fee at the counter.

items.title: Track your application
items.detail: Follow the status by the KVAC's tracking method. Don't book non-refundable flights until you're approved.

items.title: Collect your passport
items.detail: Pick it up as instructed and check the visa sticker details (name, dates, entry type) the moment you receive it.

documents.title: Document checklist — with where & how to get each
documents.intro: This is the part every other site skips. For each document, here is exactly where you obtain it and what it must show.

rows.how: Valid 6+ months beyond your trip, with at least 2 blank pages. Bring old passports too if you have them.
Complete on the Korea Visa Portal in English or Korean, print and sign. Handwritten forms are refused from 1 April 2026. One per applicant.
Plain white background, taken within the last 6 months, full face, no glasses or headwear.
A confirmed reservation/itinerary is enough — do NOT buy a paid ticket before the visa is approved.
Confirmed hotel bookings covering your stay. Staying with someone? Add an invitation letter + host's ID/ARC copy.
A 6-month statement with the bank's seal. It does NOT need to be translated into Korean. A steady balance is far more convincing than a sudden deposit.
Employed: employment/leave letter. Self-employed: business registration. Student: enrolment certificate. Retired: pension proof.
A short letter stating trip purpose and dates plus a day-by-day plan. Not always mandatory, but it strengthens a tourist file.

funds.title: "How much bank balance do I need?"
funds.body: There is no single official minimum published for the tourist visa. What matters is proving you can comfortably fund the whole trip and have reasons to return to Mongolia. Case officers look at stability, not just a headline number.
tips: Show a consistent balance over 6 months — a large deposit made days before applying looks weak.
Pair the bank statement with proof of your job, business or studies; together they tell a credible story.
Being sponsored? Add the sponsor's bank statement, a signed sponsorship letter, and proof of your relationship.

items.d: From 1 April 2026 the application form must be typed and printed. A handwritten one is refused at the counter.
A sudden large deposit right before applying. Show steady, explainable funds instead.
Paying for non-refundable tickets before approval. A reservation is enough for the file.
Only visa.go.kr (form) and the official KVAC visaforkorea.mn handle Korea visas — ignore look-alike sites that charge extra.
Wrong size, colored background, glasses or an old photo. Use a fresh 35×45 mm white-background shot.

items.q: Do Mongolian citizens need a visa for Korea?
items.a: Yes — for tourism you apply in advance for the C-3-9 short-term tourist visa. Mongolian passports are not visa-free and not on the K-ETA list.
At the Korea Visa Application Center (KVAC) in Ulaanbaatar (visaforkorea.mn), which handles applications for the Korean Embassy. You fill the form on the Korea Visa Portal, visa.go.kr.
Usually about 5–15 business days, and longer during peak season or if extra checks are needed. Apply well ahead of your trip.
Around US$40 for a single-entry short-term visa, plus the center's service fee. Amounts change and vary by visa type — confirm the current fee at visaforkorea.mn.

items.q: Does my bank statement need a Korean translation?
items.a: No — the 6-month bank statement does not need to be translated into Korean, although some other documents may need translation. Check the current document list at the KVAC.

items.q: Can I hand in a handwritten form?
items.a: No. Since 1 April 2026 the application form must be completed on a computer, printed and signed. Handwritten forms are not accepted.

items.q: Can I get a multiple-entry visa?
items.a: Multiple-entry tourist visas are possible in some cases (for example with a strong travel history), but eligibility varies. Ask at the KVAC or the embassy about current rules.

items.q: Do I still need the e-Arrival Card after I get the visa?
items.a: The e-Arrival Card requirement can still apply on entry. Check the entry-document rules close to your travel date on the official sites.
